name: Sgt. Lowry (or Lowery)
role: Special Forces sergeant on the mountain
summary: A Special Forces sergeant Larry remembers on top of Núi Bà Đen. "Kennedy pretty much ran the camp. When he was gone, Lowry ran the camp." Lowry is the man Larry told about the enemy digging on his last day there, and the man who came back and said, in Larry's words, "You son of a bitch you killed 450 civilians down there!" Larry thinks what followed came from him: "Somebody up there, probably Sgt Lowery, probably reported me KIA. All the officers were gone, so he was the only one on the other radio in Special Forces that I know of." Off duty, Larry would meet him at the Papallon on Tu Do street in Saigon: "That was the bar special forces hang out and I would meet Lowry there if he was off duty and in town. Lowry usually worked at Body Jab 42 Nui Ba Den." On a patrol, Larry says, it was Lowry who found the prisoner in VN-0023: "This guy was found in a hut by Sargent Lowry and they came out dragging him."
researchNotes: The spellings are his son's transcriptions of the name as Larry says it; neither is Larry's own rendering. The KIA connection is Larry's inference, not an established fact, and is recorded that way: he says "probably" twice in one sentence, and reasons to it from who else could have been on a radio that day rather than from anything he witnessed. It matters because it is the first mechanism the archive has for how a false report could have been generated at all, but it should not harden into a claim about a named man without documentary support. Negative (2026-09-02): asked whether Lowry's name was painted on the rock in VN-0035, Larry said no (giscus-vn-0035-c18259268), so the rock is not a route to identifying him. Negative (2026-09-09): every Lowery, Lowry and Lowrey in the complete national casualty roll (twenty-one men) was checked and none could be this man, so he is presumed alive, consistent with Larry, who never says he died; casualty and memorial sources are closed for him, and the search was redirected to rosters, unit associations and veteran registries (research/people/sgt-lowry-search.md, issue #12). A personal remark Larry made about Lowry (giscus-stories-c18259589) was moved out of this record on 2026-09-14 to that file. The accusation day is data/timeline/1965-08-450-civilians-accusation.json. 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0023-c18415971): Lowry is not said to be in the VN-0023 frame and the photograph is not linked to this record; the account places him on patrol off the summit, not only on the radio.
